# Contract check: the immediate-return remember

**Date:** 2026-04-06
**Participants:** Wynn Castellano (Staff Engineer)

Wynn: "We ratified the async job contract: remember returns a receipt in
seconds and the extraction is watched by polling a cursor. No blocking
call, and no lost work if the client drops the receipt."

Key decision: remember dispatches, then the agent either polls the run or
gets the reaction piggybacked on a later call.

positions.name: AsyncRememberContract
positions.frame: How should remember hand extraction off to the background so the caller is never blocked and no work is lost when the client drops its receipt?
positions.why: The three statements read one design direction: remember returns a receipt immediately, extraction is watched by a polling cursor (src-2), the call never blocks and work survives a dropped receipt (src-3), and the dispatch model is settled as dispatch-then-observe, with the agent either polling the run or receiving the reaction piggybacked on a later call (src-4). src-2 names polling alone, while src-4 offers piggybacked reaction as a second route; that difference is left open rather than resolved. src-2 and src-3 are attributed to Wynn Castellano and src-4 to the memo author, so the decision is carried by two voices.

placements.title: From blocking extraction to receipt-and-observe
placements.frame: What does the caller hold after dispatch, and how does it observe background work without waiting on it or losing it when its receipt is dropped?
placements.why: The position holds that remember returns a receipt in seconds, extraction is watched by a polling cursor, the call never blocks, work survives a dropped receipt, and the agent either polls the run or receives the reaction piggybacked on a later call. Together these state a durable pattern for handing work to the background, not a one-time event, so the theme is one future envelopes can keep feeding. The graph has no existing leaves, so nothing could be reused, and no close-but-not-exact neighbor exists, so this mint stands alone.
